\chapter{Learning Theory --- Convex Prediction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Hedge.ConvexPrediction
\section{Overview}

This module develops the \emph{convex prediction bridge} for the Hedge algorithm.
When every expert's prediction lies in a convex decision set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
and each round's loss function is convex on $S$, Jensen's inequality shows that the
loss of Hedge's weighted-average prediction is at most Hedge's abstract expected expert
loss; combining this with the abstract Hedge regret theorems yields tight, explicit
regret bounds for the real prediction-space problem.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Induced loss sequence]
\lean{inducedLoss}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq}
Given a loss function $\ell : \mathbb{R} \to \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, expert predictions
$p : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$, and a sequence of outcomes
$o : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \Omega$, the \emph{induced loss sequence} is the abstract
loss table $L : \mathrm{LossSeq}\,N\,T$ defined by $L_{t,i} = \ell(p_t(i),\, o_t)$,
i.e.\ expert $i$ at round $t$ incurs the loss its own prediction receives under the
realized outcome.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hedge weighted-average prediction]
\lean{hedgePrediction}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeDist, inducedLoss}
At each round $t \in \mathrm{Fin}\,T$, Hedge's \emph{prediction in the original
decision space} is the weighted average
\[
  \widehat{x}_t \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w^{(\eta)}_{t,i}\, p_t(i),
\]
where $w^{(\eta)}_{t,i} = \texttt{hedgeDist}\,\eta\,L\,t\,i$ are the Hedge
weights computed from the induced loss table $L$ up to (but not including) round $t$,
and $p_t(i)$ is expert $i$'s prediction at round $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cumulative loss of Hedge's predictions]
\lean{hedgePredictionCumLoss}
\leanok
\uses{hedgePrediction}
The \emph{actual cumulative prediction loss} of Hedge is
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T \;=\; \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \ell\!\left(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\right),
\]
where $\widehat{x}_t$ is the Hedge weighted-average prediction at round $t$.  This
differs from \texttt{hedgeCumLoss}: here the loss is applied to the averaged
prediction, not to a weighted average of expert losses.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted average stays in convex set]
\lean{hedgePrediction_mem}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum, hedgePrediction, inducedLoss}
\difficulty{3}
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a convex set and suppose every expert prediction
satisfies $p_t(i) \in S$ for all $t$ and $i$.  Then Hedge's weighted-average
prediction $\widehat{x}_t \in S$ for every round $t$.  The result follows because
the Hedge weights are nonneg\-ative and sum to one, so the weighted average is a
convex combination of points in $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen bridge: prediction loss bounded by Hedge loss]
\lean{hedgePrediction_loss_le_hedgeLoss}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum, hedgeLoss, hedgePrediction, hedgePrediction_mem, inducedLoss}
\difficulty{4}
Under the same hypotheses as above, assume additionally that for each round $t$ the
map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$.  Then Jensen's inequality gives, for
every $t$,
\[
  \ell\!\left(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\right)
  \;\le\;
  \texttt{hedgeLoss}\,\eta\,L\,t
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i} w^{(\eta)}_{t,i}\,\ell(p_t(i),\, o_t).
\]
That is, the loss of the averaged prediction is at most the Hedge-weighted average of
the individual expert losses.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cumulative Jensen inequality]
\lean{hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss}
\leanok
\uses{hedgeCumLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss, hedgePrediction_loss_le_hedgeLoss, inducedLoss}
\difficulty{2}
Summing the per-round Jensen bound over all $T$ rounds, we obtain
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T
  \;\le\;
  \texttt{hedgeCumLoss}\,\eta\,L,
\]
i.e.\ the actual cumulative loss of Hedge's convex-combination predictions is at most
the abstract cumulative Hedge loss on the induced expert loss table.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Tight regret bound for convex prediction]
\lean{hedgePrediction_regret_bound_tight}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq.Valid, bestExpertLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss, hedge_regret_bound_tight, inducedLoss, regret}
\difficulty{4}
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be convex, $\eta > 0$, and suppose all expert predictions
lie in $S$, each round loss is convex on $S$, and the induced loss table is valid.
Then the regret of Hedge's actual weighted-average predictions satisfies
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T
    - \min_{i}\,\sum_{t} \ell(p_t(i),\, o_t)
  \;\le\;
  \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta T}{8}.
\]
The proof combines the cumulative Jensen bound with the abstract tight Hedge regret
theorem \texttt{hedge\_regret\_bound\_tight}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Optimal-rate regret bound for convex prediction]
\lean{hedgePrediction_regret_tight_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq.Valid, bestExpertLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss, hedgePredictionCumLoss_le_hedgeCumLoss, hedge_regret_tight_optimal, inducedLoss, optimalEtaTight, regret}
\difficulty{4}
Under the same convexity hypotheses, with $T > 0$, $N > 1$, and the learning rate set
to $\eta^* = \texttt{optimalEtaTight}\,N\,T$, the regret satisfies
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T
    - \min_{i}\,\sum_{t} \ell(p_t(i),\, o_t)
  \;\le\;
  \sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\ln N}.
\]
\end{theorem}
